description: Outdoor display. Museum placard credits this airframe with shooting down an F-4E on 5 July 1972. Photographed in the museum park, April 2025.

Outdoor display, labelled by the museum as the MiG-21 that shot down a B-52 on the night of 27 December 1972 and wearing the number 5121. The airframe recognised as national treasure MiG-21 5121 (Pham Tuan's aircraft) is held by the Vietnam Military History Museum, so one of the two carries the other's markings; tail_number left blank because the true identity of this airframe cannot be established. Photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display, photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display, photographed April 2025. Second Su-22 in the park.
Outdoor display, photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display; heavy-lift helicopter of the VPAF. Photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display; museum labels it as the VIP transport used by President Ho Chi Minh and the Politburo. The Mi-4 cabin seat used by Ho Chi Minh is also displayed indoors. Photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display, photographed April 2025. Distinct from the Mi-24A numbered 7403 at the Southern Air Force Museum in Ho Chi Minh City.
Shipborne anti-submarine helicopter; outdoor display, photographed April 2025. Distinct from Ka-25BSh 7509 at the Vietnam Naval Museum in Hai Phong.
Outdoor display, photographed April 2025.
Chinese-built MiG-19; the museum credits this airframe with shooting down three A-4s. Some sources list it simply as a MiG-19. Photographed April 2025.
Outdoor display. Reported as wearing 2011; that number is also attributed to a Shenyang J-5 elsewhere in compiled listings, so tail_number is left blank.

Ex-VNAF airframe captured in 1975 and displayed outdoors; photographed April 2025 wearing the number 7579. The Southern Air Force Museum in Ho Chi Minh City displays an F-5 that Vietnamese press reporting in 2025 also numbers 7579, so one of the two is a repaint; tail_number left blank.
Ex-VNAF Huey captured in 1975; outdoor display, photographed April 2025. Some captions call it a UH-1A; the airframe is a UH-1H.

Ex-VNAF Skyraider displayed outdoors wearing 132, photographed April 2025. Compiled listings variously call it an AD-6 or AD-1H; A-1H (AD-6) is the correct designation for the type. The US Navy BuNo is not established.
Ex-VNAF liaison aircraft displayed behind the Skyraider, photographed April 2025 wearing 764. The Southern Air Force Museum also displays a U-17 numbered 764, so tail_number is left blank here.

Ex-VNAF A-37 captured in 1975. VOV reporting (2025) states an A-37 of the Quyet Thang (Determined to Win) squadron that bombed Tan Son Nhat on 28 April 1975 is displayed at this museum; the Southern Air Force Museum separately displays A-37B 0475 from the same action, so no number is asserted here.
Wreckage of a downed Bird Dog displayed as a war relic, not a complete airframe.
aliases: O1; O 1; L-19; Bird Dog; L19

description: Wreckage: forward fuselage and cockpit section of a downed F-4, displayed with recovered B-52 and F-4 engines. Sources differ on whether it is an F-4B or F-4D; the serial cited in compiled listings (153001) is not corroborated and is not recorded here.
Wreckage of a downed US reconnaissance drone (Ryan Firebee / AQM-34 family) displayed as a war relic.
Vietnamese-designed light trainer/liaison aircraft; museum caption records a first flight on 24 September 1980.
Vietnamese-designed light trainer; museum caption records a first flight on 24 June 1984.
Vietnamese-designed light trainer prototype; museum caption records a first flight on 24 April 1986.
Vietnamese-built light amphibious/floatplane communications microlight, displayed indoors/outdoors at the museum.
Czechoslovak-built trainer used by the early VPAF; number as listed in compiled sources, not independently confirmed from a photograph.
SA-2 Guideline surface-to-air missile with launcher; the museum displays the launcher credited with the first B-52 shootdown of December 1972 together with V-750 rounds.
aliases: SA-2; SA2; Guideline; V-750; S75; V750

description: AA-2 Atoll infrared air-to-air missile displayed with the MiG exhibits.
AA-1 Alkali beam-riding air-to-air missile displayed with the MiG exhibits.
